body.statement: If \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\), then for every \(\varepsilon\ge0\), \(\Pi_P\) maps \(\mathcal C_P^{\varepsilon}\) into \(\mathcal C_P\) and \(\|v-\Pi_P(v)\|_\infty\le\varepsilon\). The constant one is sharp. For every component-respecting mesh, the uniform-norm Hausdorff distance satisfies \(d_H(\mathcal C_{P,h},\mathcal C_P)=e_h\); hence each signed support value over \(\mathcal C_{P,h}\) differs from its full-class counterpart by at most \(\|\nu_P\|_{\mathrm{TV}}e_h\).
body.justification: Exact clipping replaces uncheckable strict-feasibility and active-set assumptions by a global deterministic stability certificate.
body.gap: Generic LP perturbation theory begins from a finite program and does not give this constant-one continuum feasibility retraction.
body.consumer: The certificate makes support gridding auditable and allows conservative endpoint computation even at equality constraints.
